transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I guess I came in because... I just can't shake this feeling that everything going wrong is my fault. Like, at work, I feel like I'm a terrible employee, and at home, I just feel like a bad homeowner. It's like I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been a few weeks, or has this been going on for months or even years?
It's definitely been going on for years. Um, I think this depression, and just the total loss of interest in everything... it's been with me for about two years and a month now.

Over these past two years, has your low mood been present nearly every day without a break, or have there been periods—weeks or months—where you felt back to your normal self before the sadness returned?

Looking back at the last couple of years, the low mood and that loss of interest have been there for almost the whole time since this all started. There haven't really been any long breaks... just maybe some brief periods where I could function a little better, but the sadness is pretty much always there nearly every day.

During these two years, have there been times when your mood and other symptoms became noticeably worse or more severe than your usual baseline, lasting at least two weeks, compared to other times when the depression felt more mild or manageable?

Um, I'm not really sure. I mean, it's hard to tell if there were specific times when it got worse for a couple of weeks. It just feels like it's been pretty constant the whole time. I haven't really noticed any big dips or anything like that, just the same heavy feeling.
During this two-year period, have you ever had thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or wishing you were dead?

No, I haven't really had thoughts like that. I mean, I feel heavy and tired all the time, but I haven't wanted to hurt myself or... or wished I wasn't here. It's just more of a constant exhaustion, I guess, not really wanting to die.
During this time, have you noticed significant changes in your sleep or appetite, or trouble concentrating, that occur along with the low mood?

Well, my sleep has definitely been a problem. Most nights, I just... I lie awake for hours, just listening to the house settle. And then when I finally do drift off, I end up waking up around three or four in the morning. After that, I just can't get back to sleep before I have to get up for work. Um, I haven't really noticed a huge difference with my appetite or anything, but the lack of sleep is pretty constant.
Have you noticed trouble concentrating or making decisions, like at work or when reading, along with these other symptoms?

Um, no, not really. I mean, work can be busy, but I haven't noticed any real trouble concentrating or anything. I can still read and get my tasks done fine. It's just the tiredness that bothers me, not really my focus.

Would you say these feelings have significantly interfered with your ability to function at work or in your relationships, or have you generally been able to keep up with your usual responsibilities despite feeling this way?

Well, it's definitely made things harder. I mean, I'm still working, but it takes so much more effort just to keep up with the basics. I've been making enough mistakes lately that my supervisor actually started checking in on my performance, which... isn't great. And outside of work, I've been missing social plans because I just don't have the energy. Even my townhouse... I've let it get way messier than I can usually stand. So, yeah, I guess it has interfered a fair amount.

Has there ever been a stretch of at least two weeks during these two years when your symptoms were clearly more intense than your usual baseline—for example, feeling even more hopeless, needing much more effort to function, or noticing several new symptoms all at once?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, it's pretty much just been this constant... low level of feeling drained and tired. I haven't really had a period where it suddenly got way worse or where I felt like everything was crashing down all at once. It's just been steady, you know? Just kind of a struggle every day, but not like a sudden spike in how bad it is.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a chronic depressive mood state lasting over two years (2 years, 1 month) that has been present nearly continuously, with only brief periods of partial relief and no clear 2-week periods of remission. Associated symptoms include persistent low energy/fatigue, sleep disturbance (initial and middle insomnia), and pervasive feelings of worthlessness/excessive self-blame. Despite chronicity, the patient explicitly denies any distinct 2-week period of symptom escalation meeting full Major Depressive Episode criteria (no anhedonia-driven functional collapse, no suicidal ideation, no concentration/appetite disturbance, no discrete worsening phase), arguing against superimposed MDD (which would suggest double depression, F33.x) or a single depressive episode (F32.x). The chronic, low-grade, non-episodic course lasting >2 years without clear MDE superimposition is most consistent with Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia), F34.1.
